content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Analysis of the test image:**

**Affected plant part:** Leaves (appears to be tomato plant based on leaf morphology)

**Key visual features observed:**
- White, fluffy/powdery patches scattered across the upper surface of the leaves
- Patches are irregular in shape and distribution
- Underlying leaf tissue remains relatively dark green — no major yellowing or necrosis
- The white growth appears superficial, sitting on top of the leaf surface
- Multiple leaves affected with similar symptoms

**Reasoning through candidate classes:**

- **Powdery Mildew**: Classic presentation is white powdery/fluffy colonies on the upper leaf surface of otherwise green leaves. The patches here match this very well — white, superficial, distributed across green leaf tissue without major tissue death beneath.
- **Gray Mold**: Would appear gray/brown and typically associated with dying/necrotic tissue, not matching here.
- **Leaf Mold**: Usually presents as yellow patches on upper surface with olive-brown/gray growth on the underside; doesn't match the white upper-surface colonies seen.
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch / Early Blight / Target Spot**: All would show distinct necrotic lesions with defined borders, not fluffy white growth.
- Bacterial and viral diseases would not produce white fluffy surface growth.

The white, cottony/powdery superficial growth on the upper surface of green tomato leaves is the hallmark presentation of **Powdery Mildew**.
